subject: Residency guarantee + temporary routing/backstop exceptions
messages:
From: Eva Lang <eva.lang@fintechco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T07:16:00Z
Subject: Residency assurance — can you confirm EU-only for production?

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood for a product that will handle EU customer PII and need a concrete answer on residency. Two specific asks:

1) Can you confirm that for an "EU-pinned" account all inference, model state (KV caches), payloads, and retention logs remain in the EU (no content leaves EU)?
2) If Redwood ever needs to route traffic cross-region (failover, monitoring, analytics aggregation), what exactly is permitted and how is it controlled? We need limits and a contractual commitment — not just an engineering note.

Also: please send the DPA and the subprocessors list and any evidence (diagram or SOC2) that shows where logs and metrics live.

We're under a contracting timeline (procurement) and legal wants the full picture before we start pilots.

Thanks,

Eva Lang
Director of Product
FintechCo

--
Requested attachments: none (please attach your DPA + diagrams)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eva Lang <eva.lang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency assurance — can you confirm EU-only for production?

Hi Eva — thanks, great questions and I appreciate the timeline. Short answer: for EU-pinned accounts production inference and persistent artifacts are kept in-region; I'll loop in Legal for the contractual language and will attach evidence.

Quick details while we pull docs:
- Model inference, the persistent store for user data, and primary logs for request/response retention are hosted in EU regions for accounts that choose EU pinning.
- We do have platform-level telemetry and aggregated metrics used for reliability and capacity planning that are processed in a separate analytics pipeline. By default that pipeline transits through our control plane and a metrics aggregator hosted in the US. The metrics are pseudonymized and token-level content is never stored in that pipeline.
- There are two cases where cross-region processing can happen:
  * Failover/Capacity: brief traffic routing to a compatible region for up to the window required to restore service (we can quantify).
  * Ops/Debugging: in emergency troubleshooting we may transfer a minimal set of traces; such transfers are logged and require escalation.

I know that might not be enough for procurement — looping Neha (Head of Legal) to provide DPA language and the subprocessors list / SOC2 copy. I'll attach the DPA and a redacted dataflow diagram in a follow-up.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement/legal through this?

Best,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

--
Attachment references to follow: DPA, dataflow diagram, SOC2

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eva Lang <eva.lang@fintechco.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, legal@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-03-22T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency assurance — can you confirm EU-only for production?

Hi Eva — good to meet you over email. I'm Neha, Head of Legal. Attaching our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v1.4.pdf), our SOC 2 Type II summary and a redacted data flow diagram (redwood-dataflow-eu-only.png). See key points below — I've written these so your procurement/legal team can drop them into contractual redlines if helpful.

Summary commitments for an EU-pinned production account:
- Primary inference, model state (including KV caches), and persisted request/response logs are stored and processed in the EU. We will not write customer content to non-EU persistent stores for pinned accounts.
- Short-lived in-memory processing may occur outside the region for routing or third-party acceleration only in explicit failover scenarios; such traffic is transient and not persisted.
- Metrics & aggregated telemetry: by default, anonymized and aggregated metrics are exported to our platform analytics cluster (US) for service-wide health. We offer an EU-only telemetry configuration for customers on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Subprocessors: list included in the DPA exhibit; key ones for EU are: EU-cloud-provider (compute/storage), monitoring-provider-eu (metrics retention), and logging-archive-eu (30-day retention by default).

Contractual language options we can provide:
1) EU-only residency clause: Redwood shall process and store customer content and logs exclusively in the EU for the term of the agreement for accounts designated EU-pinned.
2) Limited cross-border exception: in the event of force majeure or capacity failover, Redwood may route traffic outside the EU for the minimum period necessary to restore service; such incidents shall be limited to no more than 0.5% of total requests per calendar month and logged with customer notice within 48 hours. (We can negotiate the percentage or remove the exception for Dedicated/Private.)
3) Audit & evidence: Redwood will provide SOC2 reports and a redacted dataflow diagram; full audit access is available under an enterprise agreement.

If you want a stronger guarantee (no cross-border exceptions), we can propose contractual language for Dedicated or Private deployment paths that remove the failover clause and mandate EU-only telemetry. That will change delivery/price and we can put that into the quote.

Next steps
- I've attached the DPA and SOC2. Please review.
- If acceptable, Jonas can schedule a short call with engineering to validate the implementation details (dataflow diagram attached).
- If FintechCo needs DocuSign-ready language, we can prepare a DPA addendum with the specific residency/backstop text.

Regards,

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.4.pdf, SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf, redwood-dataflow-eu-only.png

From: Eva Lang <eva.lang@fintechco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, legal@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-03-22T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency assurance — can you confirm EU-only for production?

Neha / Jonas — thanks for the fast follow-up and for sending the documents. A few quick clarifications so our procurement can move forward:

1) The limited cross-border exception above is the main blocker. Can Redwood:
   - Lower the quantitative allowance to 0.1% (we can justify this to internal security if you provide monitoring/notice guarantees), or
   - Alternatively, confirm that Dedicated removes the exception and provide ballpark pricing?
2) For metrics: can you confirm what fields are included in the "anonymized" exports? We need assurance that any token-level hashes or request ids that can be re-linked are excluded.
3) Please provide a DocuSign link or redline we can sign for the DPA addendum that includes either the 0.1% allowance or the Dedicated-no-exception path.

We'll plan a brief call tomorrow to go through the DPA. If you can drop the DocuSign link before then that will speed procurement.

Best,

Eva Lang
Director of Product, FintechCo
